document_topic: Role of microglia TRPV1 in apolipoprotein E4 associated Parkinson's disease

metadata.institution: Department of Pharmacology and Chemical Biology, School of Basic Medical Sciences, Shanghai Jiaotong University, Shanghai 201318, China

objective_evidence.content: To investigate the regulation of microglia transient receptor potential vanilloid subtype 1 (TRPV1) on the pathological process of apolipoprotein E4 (ApoE4)-related Parkinson's disease (PD).

methods_evidence.content: APOE3/Trpv1flox/flox (E3/Trpv1f/f), APOE4/Trpv1flox/flox (E4/Trpv1f/f) and microglia-specific Trpv1 knockout mice Cx3cr1Cre (E4/Trpv1MGKO) were bred and injected with human A53T α-synuclein (AAV-hα-syn) into the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNpc).

After 30 days, motor function, coordination, and muscle endurance were evaluated using the open field test, traction test, pole test, rotarod test, and tail suspension test, while spatial learning and memory were assessed using the Morris water maze test.

Immunofluorescence technique was used to detect survival of dopaminergic neurons and pathological α-syn deposition in the SNpc using tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) and phosphorylated Ser129 α-synuclein [p-α-syn (Ser129)] antibodies.

results_evidence.content: E4/Trpv1MGKO (AAV-hα-syn) mice exhibited increased mean velocity and total distance in open field tests, significantly prolonged time to turn and time for lateral ambulation in pole tests, shortened latency to remain on the rotarod, and induced stronger dystonic postures during tail suspension, indicating aggravated motor dysfunction in ApoE4-associated PD mice.

Morris water maze demonstrated that E4/Trpv1MGKO (AAV-hα-syn) mice exhibited significantly prolonged escape latency and a reduced proportion of travel distance in the target quadrant, indicating that TRPV1 deficiency in microglia significantly impaired spatial learning ability in ApoE4-associated PD mice.
Immunofluorescence revealed that the loss of dopaminergic neurons in the SNpc was aggravated in E4/Trpv1MGKO (AAV-hα-syn) mice, and the p-α-syn deposition in the SNpc was increased.
The phagocytosis of microglia in the mesencephalon was enhanced, and the accumulation of lipid droplets was increased.

conclusion_evidence.content: TRPV1 deficiency in microglia accelerates the pathological progression of ApoE4-associated PD and disrupts lipid metabolic homeostasis in microglia.

background_evidence.content: Apolipoprotein E (ApoE) is a major lipid transporter in the brain, with 3 common alleles: APOE2, APOE3 and APOE4. APOE4 is closely related to accelerated decline of cognitive function and early onset of dementia in PD patients.

Transient receptor potential vanilloid 1 (TRPV1) is a ligand-gated non-selective cation channel with neuroprotective effects and shows potential as a therapeutic target in neurodegenerative diseases. TRPV1 participates in microglia-mediated inflammation and regulates microglial functions including phagocytosis and cytokine production.

statistical_evidence.content: E4/Trpv1f/f (AAV-hα-syn) mice showed a higher average speed (P = 0.007) in open field experiment. E4/Trpv1MGKO (AAV-hα-syn) mice showed further increased average speed and travel distance (both P < 0.05).

pathological_mechanisms.content: Microglia-specific Trpv1 knockout significantly increased the accumulation of lipid droplets in the microglia of PD mice induced by ApoE4, but had no significant effect on the accumulation of lipid droplets in neurons and astrocytes.
Deletion of TRPV1 enhanced ApoE4-induced phagocytosis of p-α-syn by mesencephalic microglia in PD mice.

ps3_considerations.evidence: Study provides direct functional evidence showing TRPV1 deficiency in microglia accelerates PD pathology
ps3_considerations.strength: Strong experimental evidence with multiple validation methods

ps3_considerations.evidence: Demonstrates disruption of lipid metabolic homeostasis and enhanced phagocytosis as mechanisms
Uses genetically engineered mouse models with specific cell-type knockout
ps3_considerations.strength: Validated animal model with appropriate controls

ps3_considerations.evidence: Reports statistically significant results with P-values

clinical_relevance.implications: Potential therapeutic target for ApoE4-associated PD
